ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Thomas Jefferson

code.originalText: Three-month review: response to prevention, disability, acute medicine use and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Mr. Jefferson returns twelve weeks after starting propranolol and eight weeks after raising it to 120 mg. His diary shows 3 migraine days in the past four weeks and one in the four weeks before that, with no attack lasting more than a day; each was treated with sumatriptan and naproxen, and he was pain-free within two hours in two of the three. Acute medicine was used on 3 days. He has had no tiredness, dizziness or wheeze, and his fingers are cold only on cool mornings. His mood is good. He saw the hand therapist five weeks ago, wears a wrist splint for long writing and now writes for about two hours with breaks. His HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests from the preventive visit were nonreactive and his FIT was negative, and he was told by phone. [S]

list.item:
Migraine without aura on propranolol (G43.009). A good response: monthly migraine days down from 13 to 3, more than the 50% reduction sought, with MIDAS 39 to 13 and HIT-6 66 to 54. The MIDAS still counts the end of the spring bout in its three-month recall. Propranolol 120 mg is well tolerated. Acute medicine on 3 days a month, far within the overuse limits. PHQ-9 3 on propranolol. [S]
Continue propranolol 120 mg each evening for six to twelve months, then discuss a slow taper if he stays well.
If a bout breaks through, a CGRP monoclonal antibody is the next option.
Continue sumatriptan with naproxen as needed and the diary.

Stiff right wrist after an old dislocation (M25.631). Hand therapy, a splint and dictation have lengthened his writing time to about two hours. [S]
Continue the home exercises and the splint for long writing.

list.item: A two-week headache diary that allows a firm diagnosis. Outcome by 2026-05-21: Diary of 14 days kept; ICHD-3 criteria for migraine without aura met; no red flags [S]

Monthly migraine days reduced by at least half within three months of starting prevention. Outcome by 2026-08-13: From 13 migraine days in the four weeks before prevention to 3 in the last four weeks [S]

Acute medicine on no more than two days a week, so that medication overuse headache does not develop. Outcome by 2026-08-13: Acute medicine on 3 days in the last four weeks; no combination analgesic or caffeine pill since intake [S]
Pain-free within two hours of acute treatment in most attacks. Outcome by 2026-08-13: Pain-free at two hours in 6 of 8 attacks treated with sumatriptan and naproxen since the consultation [S]
Lower headache-related disability. Outcome by 2026-08-13: MIDAS 39 (grade IV) to 13 (grade III); the three-month recall still includes the end of the May bout [S]
Write for longer without wrist pain. Outcome by 2026-08-13: Dictation and a wrist splint for long writing; about two hours with breaks [S]
